facts.infill_context: ~97 m slumped Cambrian mudstone plus resurge deposits above diagnostic basement impact breccia/shock evidence

controls.effect_on_sr004: A genuine marine impact of almost the same mapped diameter can possess a deep true crater and a damage/fracture volume extending hundreds of metres below the seabed. A 12.5 m central core is therefore incapable of testing the expected deep impact architecture.

facts: Marine impact morphology depends strongly on water depth relative to projectile diameter.
In shallow-water regimes the water layer may only modestly reduce crater size, while rim modification and infill can occur.
Intermediate/deeper relative water depths can strongly modify final morphology through projectile deceleration and water resurge.
Weak seafloor sediments can produce strong resurge-related modification at lower relative water-depth ratios than hard-target idealizations.
controls.source: Wünnemann et al., 2010, Reviews of Geophysics

facts: Numerical and geological work shows target-water-depth/projectile-size ratio controls whether water excavation/ejecta curtains detach from seafloor crater excavation.
Marine impact can produce resurge erosion, slump blocks, sediment mobilization and crater fill that mask simple dry-target morphology.

assessment.reason: Projectile diameter and event-time water depth are both unknown; marine impacts can be heavily modified by resurge and sediment infill.
assessment.key_positive_prediction_if_impact: A deep crater-floor/damage architecture and impact-derived lithologies should exist well below the superficial 12.5 m core interval, even if the visible bowl is sediment-modified.
assessment.key_negative_prediction_if_no_deep_damag: If properly resolved MCS/deep drilling shows normal undisturbed stratigraphy beneath a shallow fluid pipe/collapse feature, a hypervelocity impact origin would become strongly disfavoured.
